title: Two-sided concentration for bounded independent samples
statement: Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, let $s$ be a positive integer, and let $Y_1,\ldots,Y_s$ be independent real-valued random variables that are measurable up to null sets, take values in $[-1,1]$ almost surely, and have common mean $m$. For every $\varepsilon\ge 0$, the probability that $\left|\sum_{i=1}^s Y_i-sm\right|\ge s\varepsilon$ is at most $2\exp(-s\varepsilon^2/2)$.
hypotheses_covered: each random variable is measurable up to a null set
each random variable lies in $[-1,1]$ almost surely
replaced: Let $s>0$ be an integer and $Y_1,\ldots,Y_s$ be independent real functions on a probability space $(\Omega,\mu)$, each measurable up to a null set and valued in $[-1,1]$ almost surely, with common mean $\mathbb E Y_i=m$. Write $\Pr(A)=\mu^*(A)$ for outer probability. For every real $\varepsilon\ge0$, $\Pr[s\varepsilon\le|\sum_iY_i-sm|]\le2\exp(-s\varepsilon^2/2)$.
